result.note: Tests the Gen Z protests and Nepal's March 2026 election, Nepal's BRI accession year, and the Madhesi issue behind India's objection to Nepal's 2015 constitution.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about Nepal's general election held in March 2026:
items: It was Nepal's first election since the Gen Z-led protests that ousted Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli.
The Gen Z protests of September 2025 began as a demonstration against fuel and medicine shortages.
Balendra 'Balen' Shah, whose RSP was on track for an outright majority, had earlier been mayor of Kathmandu.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the protests began as a digital rights protest and grew into a nationwide uprising against corruption, nepotism and youth unemployment. Shah's RSP is barely three years old, so New Delhi's old playbook of working through Nepal's traditional parties will need to change.
questions.source: In September 2025, what started as a digital rights protest quickly snowballed into a nationwide uprising against corruption, nepotism, and youth unemployment.

questions.prompt: In which year did Nepal sign onto China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)?
questions.explain: Nepal joined the BRI in 2017. Chinese-built projects such as the Pokhara International Airport and the proposed Kathmandu-Tibet railway are already on the ground.
questions.source: Nepal signed onto China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) in 2017.

questions.prompt: In 2015, India objected that Nepal's new constitution failed to accommodate which community, which has ties on both sides of the India–Nepal border?
questions.explain: India said Nepal's fast-tracked 2015 constitution did not accommodate the Madhesi community. An unofficial blockade followed that choked off fuel and medicine and pushed Kathmandu towards Beijing. Balendra Shah is himself Madhesi.
questions.source: In 2015, Nepal fast-tracked a new constitution over India's objections that it failed to accommodate the Madhesi community, an ethnic group with ties on both sides of the border.
